summary: Iteration 8 — Batch C (Compatibility Timeline, First Date Script, Weekly Spark Challenge + XP). Backend: 20/20 pytest pass on real LLM + DB-manipulated streak/XP edge cases. Frontend smoke: all 5 entry-points/routes render correctly (xp_hud, tabs switch, milestone list w/ 6 items, unlocked first-date script with all 4 sections + tone, weekly-challenge-link on profile, timeline-btn + first-date-script-btn in chat header).

minor.issue: On the LLM error path, the deterministic fallback returns exactly 6 hard-coded milestones — but the spec/UX should still respect the personalization promise. If the LLM is consistently failing for a pair, the fallback gives generic content with no signal to the UI. Consider adding `fallback: true` flag so the frontend can show 'AI temporarily unavailable, showing typical timeline' instead of silently displaying canned milestones.

When the calling user has xp == 0, my_rank is null. That's acceptable for ranking-not-applicable, but the field should be documented; right now the UI handles null OK but a comment in OpenAPI would help.

When completing a non-active challenge (one of the other 11 in WEEKLY_CHALLENGES that isn't this week's), XP is still awarded but streak/last_streak_week are NOT updated (correct). The response field `streak_weeks` returns the user's CURRENT streak (`user.get('streak_weeks',0)`), which is fine — but there's no signal back to UI that this completion didn't count toward the streak. Add `counted_for_streak: bool` to make the contract explicit.

Items are returned with full internal fields (`id`, `was_active_week`, `xp_awarded`, etc.) — fine, but ALSO exposes the `user_id` field on every row (returned by `{'_id':0}` projection but `user_id` is kept). Cosmetic; redact `user_id` since the caller already knows.

issues: When user has 0 completions, shows 'No challenges completed yet.' which is correct, but the XP HUD still shows their current XP/level/streak from completions whose rows were deleted (orphan state visible). Consider showing a hint 'Earn more by completing this week's challenge'.

frontend_smoke.console_errors: None except a benign WebSocket connection log line — no JS error/exception, no .error elements detected on chat screen.

action_items: (OPTIONAL minor) Add `counted_for_streak` bool to POST /api/challenges/{id}/complete response so UI can show 'completed but didn't count toward streak' if the user picked a non-active challenge.
(OPTIONAL minor) Add `fallback: true` flag to timeline/first-date-script responses when LLM fails so frontend can mark canned content distinctly.

(NOTE for next agent) demo1's prior completion of wc11 in current week (W22) was deleted as part of test cleanup, so /api/challenges/history now returns []. demo1 user-doc xp/streak_weeks were restored via backup; only the challenge_completions row is gone. If a future test needs that row, re-insert via POST /api/challenges/wc11/complete as demo1.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now 3228 lines — Batch C added ~370 lines on top of already-flagged size issue. Router split is overdue.
WEEKLY_CHALLENGES list is hard-coded inline in server.py — move to a constants module (same comment given for PERSONALITY_QUESTIONS in iter7).

_xp_to_level uses a hard-coded thresholds list and a manual loop; consider bisect.bisect_right for clarity + perf — and clamping `level` to len(levels)-1 explicitly (currently relies on the 'if level+1<len(levels)' branch).
_active_challenge picks WEEKLY_CHALLENGES[week % 12] — across years this means W22-2026 and W22-2027 give the same challenge. Spec-OK but worth documenting.

Compatibility timeline + first-date-script LLM calls block the request thread (no timeout, no background). On slow LLM days the user sees 60-120s spinner. Move to background job + status polling, same advice as iter7's selfie verify.

first_date_script sends RAW decrypted-ish message contents to GPT-4o ('snippet = ...'). In production E2E-encrypted chat, this either (a) won't have plaintext or (b) leaks chat content to OpenAI. Either fetch only metadata or document the privacy implication.
GET /api/challenges/leaderboard exposes every top-10 user's full primary photo URL — this is public for any logged-in user. Probably fine for a dating app but worth a privacy review.
compat_timelines cache key is just match_id with no version — if WEEKLY_CHALLENGES or the prompt changes, old cached timelines persist 7 days. Add a `prompt_version` field for safe invalidation.
seed_data_creation: All mutating tests back up user doc fields (xp, streak_weeks, last_streak_week, challenge_badges) and restore in finally. challenge_completions rows for the active week are delete_many'd before/after each test to ensure clean state. Compat-timeline cache for MATCH_ID is deleted before the shape test (regenerated by LLM). First-date-script cache for MATCH_ID is deleted before the unlocked test. SIDE-EFFECT: demo1's pre-existing wc11 W22 completion row was permanently deleted during cleanup — user.xp/streak restored but the completion log is gone, so /api/challenges/history returns []. To restore, POST /api/challenges/wc11/complete as demo1 (but this would also re-set xp/streak — instead, directly insert a row into db.challenge_completions if exactly preserving prior state matters).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration8.py -v` (~9s, includes 2 real LLM calls for timeline + first-date-script). Active challenge in current ISO week is determined by `WEEKLY_CHALLENGES[isoweek % 12]`. demo1↔demo2 match id: 0a019632-6f9f-45ab-8fb6-20601b4e60f3 has >10 messages so first-date-script unlocks. Both have completed Personality DNA + interests/goals so LLM has rich context. Tests use pymongo directly to set last_streak_week=last_week_key()/two_weeks_ago_key() for streak edge cases. /api/challenges/leaderboard exposes my_rank=null when my_xp==0.
